messages:
Alex Kim: Quick follow-up to the rollout RFC — I'm thinking of a small refactor we should discuss: split the decision surface (signal evaluator) from the actuator layer (routing/fallback). The goal is clearer interfaces so different teams can swap evaluators without touching actuator code.
Maya Singh: Sounds promising. Can you sketch the responsibilities you see for each side?
Alex Kim: Evaluator = ingest metrics/events, compute a risk score & command hints (quarantine, throttle, rollback confidence). Actuator = translate hints to concrete routing ops, can be local (proxy) or central (control plane).
Chris Patel: How do we keep latency-sensitive fallbacks fast if evaluator sits in control plane?
Alex Kim: Good point. Plan: keep a local fast-path actuator with a compact policy cache + precompiled heuristics. Evaluator publishes signed hints and policy updates; local actuator can act on cached hints while waiting for central confirmation.
Samira Ortiz: That implies versioned hints and TTLs. We need deterministic precedence: local cached hint v vs central hint v+1. Also safety: local should never rollback permanently without operator ack unless confidence is high.
Evelyn Zhao: Operator UX matters — we should expose a small graded action set: observe, slow-path divert, quarantine (short), automated rollback. Operators can set a per-service cool-down and an emergency hard-stop.
Alex Kim: Agreed. Thinking about pluggable evaluators: one for latency regressions, one for quality regressions (evals-based), another for infra signals (GPU OOMs). They all output a unified hint format: {"action": "quarantine|divert|rollback|noop", "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "reason": string, "ttl": seconds}.
Maya Singh: Love unified hint format. We should allow combiners — e.g., take max(confidence) or weighted sum across evaluators. Need to decide if combiner is central or local.
Chris Patel: If combiner is local we get faster decisions but risk inconsistent global view. If central, local actors get stale. Maybe hybrid: local combiner for emergency heuristics, central combiner for policy decisions and audits.
Samira Ortiz: For safety, actuators must implement a two-tier check: immediate emergency action (fast, reversible) and delayed irreversible action (like model switch). Reversible actions: divert traffic, reduce weight. Irreversible: permanent traffic cutover or model eviction.
Alex Kim: Exactly. Also propose signal provenance metadata so auditors can trace why an action happened. Hint example in YAML to illustrate:
```
hint:
  action: quarantine
  confidence: 0.86
  reason: latency_p95:+200ms;error_rate:+0.8%
  ttl: 60
  provenance: ["central-eval:v3","local-heuristic:1.2"]
```
Evelyn Zhao: Nice. What about canary/A-B specifics — per-cohort thresholds, ramp windows, and a backoff schedule for oscillation?
Alex Kim: Propose policy fields: ramp_window, stability_window, rollback_backoff_multiplier. Actuator enforces minimal dwell time to avoid flip-flop.
Maya Singh: We should standardize metric names and aggregation windows. Too many ad-hoc metrics caused a lot of confusion in past rollouts.
Chris Patel: Also consider a per-tenant budget: allowed error tokens or latency budget per day. Evaluator reduces allowed exposure when nearing budget. That ties into cost-aware rollouts.
Samira Ortiz: Implementation note: make evaluator outputs idempotent and signed so stale messages can't cause repeated rollbacks. Use monotonic hint version numbers.
Jenkins Bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for service-search v2 -> cohort=5% at 2026-03-21T17:13Z :rocket:
Alex Kim: FYI, the plan would let that bot publish cohort events and local actuator pick them up. If central evaluator sees regression, it emits a hint with action=divert and confidence -> local actuator reduces weight immediately.
Evelyn Zhao: For audits and postmortems, log both the raw signals and the derived hint decisions. Need retention policy for at least 90 days.
Maya Singh: One more tradeoff: how many evaluator types do we support in v1? I'd vote latency + infra + quality. Keep it small.
Chris Patel: Agreed. Also a migration path: current rollout controller -> new split architecture behind a feature flag, with an escape hatch to switch to legacy controller.
Samira Ortiz: Can we add a small circuit breaker heuristic: if actuator sees X rapid state changes in Y minutes, freeze further automated actions and notify oncall?
Alex Kim: Yes. Freeze + notify pattern is required. Add a simple cooldown policy: e.g., if >3 automated rollbacks in 10m then enter manual-only for 30m.
Evelyn Zhao: I'll draft an RFC appendix with the hint schema, sample actuator API (REST + gRPC), and suggested default policy values.
Alex Kim: Awesome — rough timeline: Evan (PM) approval -> prototype in eng-platform sandbox -> small canary. Any blockers?
Maya Singh: Just dependency on standardized metric schema. I'll start a cross-team doc. :+1:
Chris Patel: I'll mock the local actuator cache and TTL logic this week.
Samira Ortiz: I'll write the safety test harness for reversible vs irreversible actions.
Alex Kim: Thanks team. Filing this thread to link from the formal RFC doc. :eyes:
